geometry_screen.limit: The minimum is exact for the declared ordinary-word stencil and single-group-loss model, not a proof of the original transmission error.

floating_group_geometry.declared_model: Place the five observed floating FGFFF coordinates at every boundary of the 257-coordinate main grid; no source letters are added or removed.
floating_group_geometry.limit: Exact for the declared ordinary-word stencil and floating-group movement model; it does not establish the p192 date or prove message identity.

cross_page_association.status: Strong textual association; not an established matching source header for the unheaded parts.
source_evidence: p199 unlettered message declares 3 TLE and provides 1 TL only.
p192 provides unheaded 2 TL and 3 TL without a surviving message header on that page.
p199 1 TL asks General von Kress in Tiflis to forward a Polish Foreign Ministry telegram to WACLAW V OSTROWSKI.
p192 2 TL begins TIFLISDOPPELPUNKT and the appointment text; part 3 completes the appointment and says instructions have already been sent through a courier.
All three records decrypt under the unchanged Nov13-15b published key.
cross_page_association.date_caveat: The p199 header explicitly says November 15 / 15/11. The p192 page is headed November 14. The separate p192 A and B headers also pair November 14 receipt dates with 15/11 originating dates; these inconsistencies are preserved, not resolved here.
cross_page_association.historical_context: The independent Mądzik archival study discusses Wacław Ostrowski as a Polish representative in Tbilisi in 1918 (printed pp. 78–79). This is corroboration after the source reading, not a crib used to select the floating-group position.

conditional_key_layers.inventory_scope: All three Tiflis records and all seven source records in the November 14 retransmissions edition; every changed raw character and marginal domain is retained.

assumptions: The stated single-group gap model and ordinary-word alignment are correct.
The courier surname identifies the independently attested Tadeusz Tydelski, with its correct spelling.

layer2.additional_assumption: The p190 A and p194 B FR?E fields encode the same correctly copied surname.

limits: The independently sourced p199 part 1 is strongly associated with the unheaded p192 parts 2 and 3 by syntax, stated multipart count and key. Their conflicting November 14/15 headings remain unresolved.
The floating-group placement masks all relevant historical names and reference symbols; no historical identity was used to select it.
The missing-group minimum is conditional on a declared ordinary-word stencil. Neither courier name nor signature is used in that screen.
Historical identity is independently supported but remains an inference; the original archival manuscript and appointment telegram have not been inspected.
Reencryption alone permits all eight unused symbols in the name cell. The historical name evidence is what selects Y.
Transferring Y from Nov13–15b FX to Nov13–15a DG additionally depends on the pilot same-name assumption.
